text: if it can be detoxified and rendered safe. A multi-antigen, multistage combination vaccine is thought to be the best approach to effective vaccination against malaria. One such vaccine, SPf66, a synthetic preparation of three antigens from the asexual phase of the parasite in the blood linked by a sporozoite antigen has been studied but little or no evidence for its protective efficacy has been found.3 Another multicomponent vaccine, NYVAC-Pf7, using a recombinant vaccinia viral vector that expresses 7 proteins from different stages of malarial infec- tion, has also been studied,17 but results have been disappointing.
